sections.html:
Lawrence is a Douglas County city about 25 miles east of Topeka and 35 miles west of Kansas City, Kansas. It sits between the Kansas River and the Wakarusa River, which shapes both its streets and its flood maps. The city covers 34.26 square miles, with its highest ground on Mount Oread, where the University of Kansas campus stands at 1,020 feet.

Several creeks cross town. Burroughs Creek runs through East Lawrence, Baldwin Creek drains the northwest, and Yankee Tank Creek in the southwest feeds Lake Alvamar before reaching the Wakarusa. Add 54 parks and the planned 22-mile Lawrence Loop trail, and two houses a mile apart can sit in very different settings. Buyers notice.

Interstate 70, running here as the Kansas Turnpike, crosses the northern edge. U.S. 59 follows Iowa Street, U.S. 40 follows 6th Street, and K-10 reaches Kansas City by the South Lawrence Trafficway. Two bus systems, The T and KU on Wheels, run 18 routes. The drive to the Kansas City area is one reason owners hold a Lawrence house for years.

Antislavery settlers founded Lawrence in 1854. On August 21, 1863, William Quantrill's raiders destroyed most of the town's houses and businesses, so the oldest surviving buildings mostly date from the rebuilding that followed.

Neighborhoods close to downtown, such as Old West Lawrence, North Lawrence, East Lawrence, Oread, Hancock and Pinkney, tend to hold older homes. Farther west, past Iowa Street, are Sunset Hills, Prairie Meadows, Deerfield and Alvamar. An older house may carry original wiring, plumbing or a stone foundation, and a conventional buyer's lender and inspector will ask about each.

Education anchors the local economy. The University of Kansas was the largest employer in 2020 with 10,116 employees, followed by Maximus, Lawrence Memorial Hospital and Hallmark Cards.

A university town has its own housing rhythm. Leases turn over in summer, and the city schedules no required rental inspections in July or August unless the owner asks. If you own a rental near campus, that calendar affects when a vacant house is easiest to show or hand over.

In February 2023 the City Commission passed an ordinance banning source of income discrimination, so landlords cannot turn away housing vouchers. Anyone selling a tenant-occupied house should know the rule exists.

sections.h2: How does Lawrence weather affect a house?
sections.html:
Summers are hot and humid, winters cold and dry. The average July daily high is 88.6 F and the average January daily low is 19.4 F. Annual precipitation is 39.40 inches and snowfall 10.4 inches. The record high is 114 F, set in August 1934.

Spring is the wet season, with May near 5.13 inches and June near 5.69. Heavy rain is hard on basements, gutters and older roofs, and wide swings between freezing winters and hot summers stress siding, driveways and foundations. Those are the items an inspector writes up first, and they are the ones that pull a conventional sale into repair negotiations.

Lawrence requires a license for every rental dwelling unit in the city, renewed each year, under Ordinance 8840, adopted April 1, 2014. The city's FAQ covers points that matter to an owner who wants out:

  • Vacant rental units still need a license.
  • A house under contract to be bought by its tenant stays on the licensing rolls until the buyer's name is recorded with the Douglas County Register of Deeds.
  • If the owner lives elsewhere and a relative lives in the house, it is exempt. If that relative has an unrelated roommate, it needs a license.
  • Required inspections run on a 3-year or 6-year cycle depending on how many violations were found, and the owner or agent must attend.
  • A notice of violation generally gives 30 days to fix items, and an appeal goes to the Building Code Board of Appeals within 14 days.

Renting without a license may be prosecuted in municipal court. Occupancy limits matter too: city zoning allows up to three unrelated occupants in single-family districts and four in most other districts. An investor or heir who inherits a rental with a lapsed license or open violations can find that a normal listing stalls. A buyer who takes the house as is does not need the license fixed before closing.

Douglas County bills property tax. The treasurer's office is at 2601 West 6th Street, and the Register of Deeds is in the courthouse at 1100 Massachusetts Street. For tax questions, call the treasurer at 785-832-5178.

The treasurer's formula for a residential property: appraised value times 11.5 percent gives assessed value, and assessed value times the mill levy, divided by 1,000, gives the estimated tax. The first half is due on or before December 20.

At closing, the title company normally prorates the year's tax between buyer and seller, so ask for a payoff and proration figure early. If taxes are behind, the treasurer can explain how the county handles tax foreclosures.

The Register of Deeds records deeds, mortgages, plats and other real estate documents, and a title company or attorney usually handles the filing. Electronic recording runs through four vendors: Simplifile, Mobilis, CSC and ePN. Documents must carry the full legal description, and the office advises against abbreviated ones. The county publishes a Kansas Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire, which is how a sale price is reported.

The office does not prepare deeds and recommends a title company or attorney, since a drafting error can change ownership in ways that are costly to fix. It also runs a free Real Estate Fraud Alert service: enroll by name and get an email when a matching name is indexed. If you inherited a Lawrence house or live out of town, that is useful while the property sits vacant.

sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell?
sections.html:
Three routes are practical: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as is.

  • Listing: best when the house is in good shape and you can wait through showings, inspection requests and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Selling yourself: saves an agent's fee but puts marketing, disclosures and paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: suits a vacant rental, an inherited house, a property with code violations or a seller who needs a firm closing date.

In Lawrence, cash tends to come up with student rentals that need work after a hard lease year, inherited houses in older neighborhoods and owners who live elsewhere. Whatever the route, compare the net after repairs, carrying costs and time, not only the headline number. We buy houses in Lawrence as is, and you can request an offer without obligation.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Lawrence?
faqs.a: You need the license to keep renting, not to sell. Lawrence requires one for each rental unit, vacant ones included, until a buyer's name is recorded as owner with the Douglas County Register of Deeds. Letting it lapse while tenants remain can bring municipal court action.

faqs.q: When are Douglas County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half or the full amount is due on or before December 20. The treasurer takes payments after November 1, and tax questions go to 785-832-5178.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Lawrence house?
faqs.a: At the Douglas County Register of Deeds, 1100 Massachusetts Street in Lawrence. Title companies usually record electronically through a vendor such as Simplifile, so you seldom file the deed yourself.

faqs.q: Does the University of Kansas affect when a house sells?
faqs.a: It affects rentals most. The university is the city's largest employer, summer is the busy lease turnover period, and the city schedules no required rental inspections in July or August unless the owner asks.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lawrence house with code or inspection problems?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as is, so open violations, deferred repairs or a failed rental inspection do not have to be fixed first. A conventional buyer's lender and inspector will usually require them to be addressed.
